moments.title: When is this useful?
moments.text: A final result may need to be expressed in scientific notation, particularly for very large or very small values.

moments.title: A compact representation
moments.text: Scientific notation writes a number using a coefficient and a power of ten, avoiding long strings of zeros.

moments.title: Two contrasting examples
moments.text: The presenter moves from the definition to a large number and then a small number.

moments.title: Start with 457,000
moments.text: The decimal point of the integer is understood to be to the right of its last digit.

moments.title: Choose the coefficient
moments.text: Move the decimal point until the coefficient is between 1 and 10: $457000$ becomes $4.57$ after five places.

moments.title: Choose the exponent
moments.text: The original number is large, so the exponent is positive: $457000=4.57\times10^5$.

moments.title: Convert a small number
moments.text: The second coefficient is $5.82$. Moving the decimal point three places gives $0.00582=5.82\times10^{-3}$.

moments.title: A question requiring standard form
moments.text: The presenter moves to a question that specifies the form of the answer and asks for three significant figures.

moments.title: Interpret the notation
moments.text: The requested form is $a\times10^k$, where $1\le a<10$ and $k$ is an integer.

moments.title: Convert the value
moments.text: For $0.0286$, use the coefficient $2.86$. The decimal point moves two places and the exponent is negative, giving $2.86\times10^{-2}$.

moments.title: State the result
moments.text: The final result is $2.86\times10^{-2}$, with three significant figures.

ican.text: I can identify the coefficient and exponent in standard form and check their allowed values.
I can convert positive numbers between decimal notation and standard form.
I can calculate with numbers in standard form, including addition, multiplication and division.
I can report a result in standard form to the requested number of significant figures and include units.

ku.text: Standard form is $a\times10^k$, where $1\leq a<10$ and $k$ is an integer. For negative numbers, put a minus sign in front of the standard-form magnitude.
For a positive number greater than or equal to 10, $k$ is positive. For a positive number between 0 and 1, $k$ is negative. Numbers from 1 up to 10 have $k=0$.
For multiplication, multiply coefficients and add exponents. For division, divide coefficients and subtract exponents. Renormalize the result if the coefficient is outside $[1,10)$.
To add or subtract, first express the quantities using the same power of 10, then combine coefficients.
For positive numbers written with normalized coefficients, compare the exponents first. If the exponents are equal, compare the coefficients.
When rounding makes the coefficient 10, renormalize. For example, $9.999\times10^3$ to 3 significant figures is $1.00\times10^4$.

misc.better: The coefficient must be less than 10. Write $3.24\times10^6$.
The original positive number is less than 1, so $0.0042=4.2\times10^{-3}$.

misc.weak: $0.00070=7\times10^{-4}$ is always enough to show the original precision.
misc.better: If two significant figures are intended, write $7.0\times10^{-4}$. The trailing zero records the stated precision.
Normalize the coefficient after rounding: $1.00\times10^4$ to 3 significant figures.

terms.text: Give the coefficient and power of 10, with the coefficient in the required range.
Use the calculator and report the requested accuracy, keeping extra digits during working.

formula.text: Use the exponent laws when multiplying or dividing powers of 10. Check the formula booklet for the exact permitted rules.

worked.prompt: A bacterium has a mass of $0.00000000000274$ g. A sample contains exactly $3\times10^6$ bacteria of this mass.

parts.label: (a)
parts.q: Write the mass of one bacterium in standard form.

parts.label: (b)
parts.q: Find the total mass in standard form.

parts.label: (c)
parts.q: A second sample has a mass of $1.40\times10^{-6}$ g. Find the combined mass in standard form.

kq.model: Its coefficient is 24, outside the standard-form interval. The equivalent standard form is $2.4\times10^4$.

kq.q: How can two equivalent expressions show different stated precision?
kq.model: $7\times10^{-4}$ and $7.0\times10^{-4}$ have the same numerical value, but the second explicitly shows two significant figures.

kq.q: Why can you add coefficients directly only after matching powers of ten?
kq.model: The powers of ten determine the place value of each coefficient. Once the powers match, the coefficients count the same-sized units.
